info.name: Household API
info.description:
Family finance & shopping management — automated API scenario collection (#192/#207).

## Setup
1. `docker compose up -d --wait` (postgres/redis/kafka + all 6 app services)
2. `docker compose exec -T auth-service node scripts/seed-e2e-user.js` (#204) — seeds the two users this collection logs in as
3. Import this collection and `household.postman_environment.json`, select the **Household — Local** environment
4. Run the whole collection: `pnpm test:postman`, or in the Postman app

## Auth flow
The **Setup** folder logs in both seeded users (owner + invitee) and captures their tokens/cookies. Every other request uses the `{{accessToken}}` (owner) bearer token by default; the invite-accept request overrides it per-request with `{{accessTokenInvitee}}`.

## Self-cleanup
Every entity name includes `{{runId}}` (set once per run) so repeated runs never collide, and the **Cleanup** folder deletes the household (cascading to finance + shopping) and logs out both sessions at the end. **Never run with `--bail`** — it would skip Cleanup on the first failed assertion.

## Deliberately out of scope
Registration + email verification and real OAuth consent stay a manual-only flow (#192) — the 6-digit verification code only ever exists in Redis and a service log line, and Google actively blocks scripted OAuth consent.

item.description: Credential-free scenario checks for integration-service (#20) — validation, tenant isolation, and 404 routing. A real Monobank connect + sync (valid token → client-info → statement) is deliberately manual-only here, the same carve-out this collection already makes for real OAuth consent: Monobank issues personal tokens per real bank account, so there's no scriptable credential to seed like the two e2e users below. #21's mapping endpoints are covered the same way — listing/404 paths only. A real map (an unmapped transaction created by a real sync, then linked to an account/category) needs an actual synced Monobank transaction, so it stays manual-only for the same reason.

item.description: Runs even after upstream failures where practical (guarded on householdId) — never run this collection with --bail, which would skip this folder and leak a household + two live sessions per failed run.
